title: Xcode before 27.2: an app may read arbitrary files through a symlink in CoreDevice (CVE-2026-112605), and an Instruments authorization issue (CVE-2026-112602)
summary: Apple's security notes for Xcode 27.2 (support.apple.com/en-us/149589, released 29 Oct 2026, available for macOS Tahoe 26.6 and later) name two fixes: CoreDevice, "An app may be able to read arbitrary files", addressed with improved handling of symlinks (CVE-2026-112605), and Instruments, "An app may be able to access sensitive user data", an authorization issue addressed with improved state management (CVE-2026-112602). Before it, Apple's notes for Xcode 27 (support.apple.com/en-us/149040, 14 Sep 2026) named two sandbox escapes, both "addressed by enforcing library validation on the affected binaries": App Store, "An app may be able to break out of its sandbox" (CVE-2026-86948), and Xcode, "A malicious app may be able to break out of its sandbox" (CVE-2026-86949), with three other fixes; an Xcode below 27.2 is below 27's fixes too when it is below 27. CISA's catalog (2026.11.13) lists none of them, so Wardlatch says "fixed in", not "exploited". Wardlatch reads each Xcode's version from its Contents/version.plist: every Xcode*.app in /Applications and ~/Applications (the names matched as a Mac's disk matches them), and the Xcode that xcode-select points to (/var/db/xcode_select_link), each once. It never runs Xcode or xcodebuild. Below 27.2 is EXPOSED. A beta, by the name Apple gives its folder (Xcode-beta.app, read where the path really leads), is REVIEW even at 27.2 or later: Apple's note is about the release, and a beta renamed to Xcode.app reads as its number says. Off a Mac there is no Xcode, and no row.

reviewIfRe.reason: this Xcode is a beta (its folder is named as Apple names its betas, Xcode-beta.app); Apple's note names the release 27.2, so whether this beta has the fixes is not known

versionFiles.fix: Update Xcode to 27.2 or later (App Store, or developer.apple.com/download), and remove older copies you no longer use. Xcode 27.2 needs macOS Tahoe 26.6 or later.
versionFiles.lookedIn: the version.plist of every Xcode*.app in /Applications and ~/Applications, and of the Xcode xcode-select points to

reviewFix: Install the release of Xcode 27.2 or later beside the beta, and use it for work that opens untrusted projects or devices.
notCovered: Xcode copies elsewhere (an external disk, or a folder other than /Applications and ~/Applications that xcode-select does not point to), a beta renamed so its folder no longer says beta, and the Command Line Tools, which Apple's note does not name.
